assumptions.condition: The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
The marginal law of \(X\) under \(P\) is uniform on \([0,1]\).
For every \(z\in\{0,1\}\), the map \(x\mapsto E_P[D(z)\mid X=x]\) is continuous at \(c_P\).

standard.name: Fuzzy-RD continuity of potential treatment reduced forms

assumptions.condition: For every \(z\in\{0,1\}\), the map \(x\mapsto E_P[Y(D(z))\mid X=x]\) is continuous at \(c_P\).

standard.name: Fuzzy-RD continuity of potential outcome reduced forms

assumptions.condition: For every \(V\in\{D,Y\}\) and \(\ell\in\{-,+\}\), the one-sided regression \(\mu_{V,P}^{\ell}\) admits an extension to \([0,1]\) in the radius-\(M\) H\"older ball of order \(s\), with the derivative interpreted in the standard way when \(s>1\).

novel.justification: The factor-two shell defines a strength-indexed minimax slice rather than an identifying restriction. It represents sequences of study populations whose take-up contrasts share the same empirical order, including administrative rules that become less binding in increasingly local populations.

assumptions.condition: For every \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), \(\operatorname{Var}_P(Y-\vartheta D\mid X=x)\ge v\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in[c_P-1/8,c_P+1/8]\).

standard.name: Null-residual variance nondegeneracy on a bounded inversion set, a direct specialization of the condition used to studentize \(Y-cD\)

definitions.name: \mathcal P_n
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal P_n(s,M,\kappa_n)=\{P:\text{ at index }n\text{, the properties in ass:iid-sampling, ass:uniform-running-variable, ass:interior-cutoff, ass:potential-treatment-continuity, ass:potential-outcome-continuity, ass:observable-holder-extensions, and ass:local-compliance-strength hold}\}.\] No conditional-variance, joint-cell positivity, or treatment--outcome association restriction is imposed beyond compatibility with a binary joint law and the maintained causal model.

definitions.name: L_n^\star
definitions.construction: \[L_n^\star(\kappa_n)=\inf_{I_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P[|I_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)|],\qquad \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\theta_P\in I_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\}\ge1-\alpha,\] where the infimum ranges over measurable rules whose values are connected subsets of \(\Theta\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak R
definitions.construction: For fixed \(s\in[1,2]\), partition every compliance-strength sequence after passage to a subsequence as follows: \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{flat}}=\{\tau_n\to0\}\); \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{slope}}=\{\tau_n\to\tau\in(0,\infty)\}\); \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{entropy},0}=\{\tau_n\to\infty,\lambda_n\to0\}\); \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{entropy},\lambda}=\{\tau_n\to\infty,\lambda_n\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\}\); and \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}=\{\tau_n\to\infty,\lambda_n\to\infty\}\). The cutoff-recovery predicate \(\mathsf{CR}(s,\kappa_\bullet)\) holds exactly when \(\lambda_n\to\infty\). The finite-grid upper-rate subregime is defined separately by \(\text{def:profile-resolution-schedule}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal W_n^{\mathrm{loc}}
definitions.construction: Put \(q=1/4\), \(c_0=1/2\), and \(c_t=c_0+t\kappa_n/q\). Under \(P_t\), conditionally on \(X=x\), let \(D\) and \(Y\) be independent Bernoulli variables. Let the mean of \(D\) be \((1-\kappa_n)/2\) for \(x<c_t\) and \((1+\kappa_n)/2\) for \(x\ge c_t\); let the mean of \(Y\) be \(1/2-q(x-c_0)/2\) for \(x<c_t\) and \(1/2+q(x-c_0)/2\) for \(x\ge c_t\). At \(c_t\), assign response-type masses \(P_t(R=A)=P_t(R=N)=(1-\kappa_n)/2\) and \(P_t(R=C)=\kappa_n\); give always-takers and never-takers common binary potential outcomes with respective means \((1-t\kappa_n)/2\) and \((1+t\kappa_n)/2\), and give compliers potential-outcome means \((1-t)/2\) and \((1+t)/2\). Extend away from \(c_t\) by the same type-independent binary Markov kernel on each observed side that maps the cutoff outcome mean to the declared mean of \(Y\). The resulting continuum is \(\mathcal W_n^{\mathrm{loc}}=\{P_t:t\in[-1,1]\}\).

definitions.name: \mathsf H_{\mathrm{crit}}
definitions.construction: Adapt unknown-boundary experiment comparison to the joint four-cell binary law, obtain the optimized local recovery profiles for cutoff displacement and signed effect label, truncate and renormalize translated-cutoff mixtures at the support boundary, retain every first- and second-order likelihood coordinate that survives on the \(s=1\) faces indexed by \(T_n\) and \(\tau_n\), and solve the resulting fixed-\(\alpha\) connected-interval decision problem by test inversion.

definitions.name: \mathcal Q(c,\vartheta)
definitions.construction: For \(c\in[1/4,3/4]\) and \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), \(\mathcal Q(c,\vartheta)=\{q=(q_{d,y})_{d,y\in\{0,1\}}:\ q_{d,y}:[0,1]\to[0,1]\text{ is measurable},\ \sum_{d,y}q_{d,y}(x)=1\text{ for Lebesgue-almost every }x,\text{ the two margins are restrictions of separate one-sided radius-}M\text{, order-}s\text{ H\"older extensions split at }c,\ \Delta q_D(c)\in[\kappa_n,2\kappa_n],\ \Delta q_Y(c)=\vartheta\Delta q_D(c)\}\). The coordinate \(q_{1,1}(x)\) is otherwise free over its binary Fr\'echet interval, so zero and singular cells belong to the domain.

definitions.name: \mathcal L_P(c,\vartheta)
definitions.construction: For \(c\in[1/4,3/4]\) and \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), define the four-cell Bernoulli-pair profile loss by \[\mathcal L_P(c,\vartheta)=\inf_{q\in\mathcal Q(c,\vartheta)}\int_0^1\sum_{d,y\in\{0,1\}}p_{d,y,P}(x)\log\frac{p_{d,y,P}(x)}{q_{d,y}(x)}\,dx.\] Use \(0\log(0/q)=0\), and set a summand to \(+\infty\) when \(p_{d,y,P}(x)>0=q_{d,y}(x)\). The optimization domain in \(\text{def:population-profile-domain}\) includes singular boundary cells. The reference split is the feasible pair \((c_P,\theta_P)\), for which \(\mathcal L_P(c_P,\theta_P)=0\).

definitions.name: Certified grid, sieve, and transfer schedule
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathcal G_c=\{1/4+j/[2\lceil(2\eta_{c,n})^{-1}\rceil]:j=0,\ldots,\lceil(2\eta_{c,n})^{-1}\rceil\}\) and \(\mathcal G_\vartheta=\{-1+2j/\lceil2/\eta_{\vartheta,n}\rceil:j=0,\ldots,\lceil2/\eta_{\vartheta,n}\rceil\}\). For each candidate \(c\), form \(\mathcal B_n(c)\) by adding \(c\) to the uniform knots \(j/\lceil1/b_n\rceil\). At \(s=1\), use continuous piecewise-linear inner and outer sieves; at \(1<s\le2\), use continuously differentiable piecewise-quadratic sieves with all pairwise \((s-1)\)-H\"older derivative constraints. In both cases use outer slack \(M b_n^s=\kappa_n r_n/\ell_n\). Allocate \(\delta_n=\min\{\alpha/4,r_n^2\}\) to calibration. Record separately the normalized type-and-sieve complexity \(\zeta_n=K_n\log(n|\mathcal G_c||\mathcal G_\vartheta|/\delta_n)/(n\kappa_n^2h_n)\), cutoff-label rounding \(\eta_{c,n}/\kappa_n\), effect rounding \(\eta_{\vartheta,n}\), H\"older approximation \(M b_n^s/\kappa_n\), moved-strip probability \(n\eta_{c,n}\), global false-split probability bound \(|\mathcal G_c|\exp[-C_{\mathrm{sep}}n\kappa_n^2h_n/4]\), calibration contribution \(2\delta_n\), and fallback contribution \(2\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\text{a listed fallback occurs}\}\). The first four continuum terms sum to \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cont},n}\). Define \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}=\{\kappa_\bullet\in\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}:\zeta_n\to0,\ |\mathcal G_c|\exp[-C_{\mathrm{sep}}n\kappa_n^2h_n/4]=o(r_n),\ \varepsilon_{\mathrm{cont},n}=o(r_n)\}\). These terms are not absorbed into a generic remainder.

definitions.name: \Gamma_n(\delta_n)
definitions.construction: For each \((c,\vartheta)\in\mathcal G_c\times\mathcal G_\vartheta\), use \(\mathcal B_n(c)\) and let \(\Pi_n(c,\vartheta)\) contain arrays \(\pi=(\pi_{k,d,y})\) of four nonnegative cells summing to one in every bin. Their two margins must equal bin averages of the certified outer H\"older sieves split at \(c\), satisfy the treatment-jump shell, and satisfy the null jump restriction for \(\vartheta\); the remaining association coordinate in every bin is free over its Fr\'echet interval. Put \(\widehat p_{k,d,y}(c)=N_{k,d,y}(c)/N_k(c)\) when \(N_k(c)>0\), and define \(\Delta_n(c,\vartheta)=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_n(c,\vartheta)}\sum_{k:N_k(c)>0}N_k(c)\operatorname{KL}(\widehat p_k(c),\pi_k)\). Accept the grid pair when \(\Delta_n(c,\vartheta)\le\Gamma_n(\delta_n)\), where \(\Gamma_n(\delta_n)=3\sum_{k=1}^{K_n}\log(N_k(c)+1)+\log(|\mathcal G_c||\mathcal G_\vartheta|/\delta_n)\). Use the conventions \(0\log(0/q)=0\) and \(p\log(p/0)=+\infty\) for \(p>0\). Thus the joint four-cell deviance never divides by a covariance and remains defined on every singular association face.

definitions.name: Finite-grid population profile
definitions.construction: Specialize the moving-cutoff family to \(\kappa_n=1/32\) and \(t=0\). Take \(\mathcal G_c=\{3/8,1/2,5/8\}\), \(\mathcal G_\vartheta=\{-1,0,1\}\), and the four-bin partition \([0,3/8),[3/8,1/2),[1/2,5/8),[5/8,1]\). In the cell order \((0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), the bin-average joint-cell vectors, each divided by \(8192\), are \[(1947,2277,1829,2139),\quad(2079,2145,1953,2015),\quad(1953,2015,2079,2145),\quad(1829,2139,1947,2277).\] Every vector is nonnegative and sums to one. Their treatment margins are \(31/64\) in the first two bins and \(33/64\) in the last two; their outcome margins equal \(69/128,65/128,65/128,69/128\). The unrestricted association coordinate is the displayed fourth cell in each bin. The true pair \((c,\vartheta)=(1/2,0)\) belongs to the profile domain and has population deviance zero. For this four-bin, three-by-three grid, the finite-sample threshold is \(3\sum_{k=1}^4\log(N_k(1/2)+1)+\log(9/\delta_n)\). A certified infeasible null is rejected. The rule returns \(\Theta\) under each and only each of the following fallback branches: a bin required by the certificate is empty; cutoff-grid enlargement is uncertified; effect-grid enlargement is uncertified; the inner--outer H\"older gap exceeds \(M b_n^s\); the solver fails; the reported optimum lacks a certificate; the projected treatment-jump confidence set meets \([0,\kappa_n/2]\); the universal threshold cannot be computed; or the requested \(n\), grid, or sieve is outside the deterministic schedule. Ties are resolved lexicographically.

definitions.name: \mathsf H_{\mathrm{prof}}
definitions.construction: At every \(c\in\mathcal G_c\) and \(\vartheta\in\mathcal G_\vartheta\), profile certified support-wide one-sided H\"older margins subject to \(\mu_{Y,P}^{+}(c)-\mu_{Y,P}^{-}(c)=\vartheta\{\mu_{D,P}^{+}(c)-\mu_{D,P}^{-}(c)\}\), while leaving each bin's association coordinate free over its binary Fr\'echet interval. Calibrate the complete four-cell count vector with \(\Delta_n(c,\vartheta)\) and \(\Gamma_n(\delta_n)\); use the grid and sieve schedule in \(\text{def:profile-resolution-schedule}\); invert the tests; enlarge by \(\eta_{\vartheta,n}\); and take the connected hull. Track \(\zeta_n\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cont},n}\), the displayed global false-split bound, \(2\delta_n\), and the probability of every fallback separately. Use the exhaustive fallback list in \(\text{def:worked-four-cell-grid}\), returning \(\Theta\) on every listed branch. Finite-grid validity is uniform over all compatible binary treatment--outcome associations because calibration uses multinomial type probabilities rather than an invertible joint-score covariance.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), \[d_P=P(R=C\mid X=c_P),\qquad y_P=E_P[(Y(1)-Y(0))\mathbf 1\{R=C\}\mid X=c_P],\] and therefore \(\theta_P=E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid R=C,X=c_P]\).
statements.justification: This fixes the causal interpretation before the statistical nonregularity is analyzed.
statements.gap: Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001) give the known-cutoff Wald identification argument; the proposition records the same argument on the preserved unknown-cutoff triangular class.
statements.consumer: Every later confidence interval can be interpreted as an interval for the local complier causal effect rather than only for an observable jump ratio.

statements.statement: If \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), then \(\mathcal W_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\subset\mathcal P_n\), \(d_{P_t}=\kappa_n\), and \(\theta_{P_t}=t\) for every \(t\in[-1,1]\). Moreover, \[\operatorname{KL}(P_t^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})\le32n\kappa_n^3|t|=32\tau_n|t|,\qquad \operatorname{TV}(P_t^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})\le4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}.\]
statements.justification: The continuum supplies a same-class obstruction indexed by the entire effect-label space rather than by one hand-tuned pair.
statements.gap: Tuvaandorj (2020) transfers sharp-RD cutoff-location rates through a Gaussian convolution experiment but does not construct a binary monotone-compliance lift whose causal label moves with the cutoff.
statements.consumer: The continuum determines when unknown cutoff uncertainty alone forces nearly uninformative honest LATE intervals.

statements.statement: For fixed \(s\in[1,2]\), \(\tau_n=T_n\kappa_n^{1-1/s}\), and every strength sequence has a subsequence in exactly one component of \(\mathfrak R\). If \(s=1\), then \(T_n=\tau_n\), so the finite and divergent location-entropy faces remain distinct according to \(\lambda_n=\tau_n/\log(e/\kappa_n)\). If fixed \(s>1\) and \(\lambda_n\) remains bounded, then \(\tau_n\to0\); if fixed \(s>1\) and \(\tau_n\to\infty\), then \(\lambda_n\to\infty\). Thus cutoff recovery \(\mathsf{CR}(s,\kappa_\bullet)\) does not by itself imply shrinking effect intervals. The lower comparison at scale \(r_n\) is posed on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\), while attainment by the conservative finite-grid procedure is posed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\).
statements.justification: The algebra separates global cutoff localization from the slope-induced indistinguishability that governs the causal effect label.
statements.gap: Unknown-break papers classify location recovery, but the additional identity linking \(T_n\) and \(\tau_n\) is specific to the weak fuzzy-RD effect problem.
statements.consumer: The partition tells an applied user which asymptotic statement is licensed by an estimated compliance strength and prevents use of a recovered-regime rate on a flat or critical face.

statements.statement: For \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), \[2[1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_n}]_+\le L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\le2(1-\alpha).\] Hence \(\tau_n\to0\) implies \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\to2(1-\alpha)\). If \(s>1\) is fixed and \(\lambda_n\) remains in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)\), then the same limit holds.
statements.justification: This identifies an exact nonshrinking phase and removes a spurious higher-smoothness transition based only on location entropy.
statements.gap: Mikusheva (2010) links weak-instrument test power to confidence-set length, while the banked parent obtained only a two-label location mixture; neither yields the full-label coefficient \(2(1-\alpha)\) in this unknown-cutoff class.
statements.consumer: An analyst can recognize regimes in which any apparently narrow interval must owe its informativeness to restrictions stronger than the maintained H\"older class.

statements.statement: For every \(s\in[1,2]\) and \(M\ge2\), there exists \(C_{\mathrm{sep}}=C_{\mathrm{sep}}(s,M)>0\), independent of \(n\), \(P\), \(c\), \(\vartheta\), and every conditional treatment--outcome association, such that for every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and \(c\in[1/4,3/4]\), \[\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\left\{\mathcal L_P(c,\vartheta)-\mathcal L_P(c_P,\theta_P)\right\}\ge C_{\mathrm{sep}}\kappa_n^2\min\{|c-c_P|,h_n\}.\] Here \(\mathcal L_P\) is the four-cell Bernoulli-pair loss in \(\text{def:population-profile-loss}\), its optimization runs over all \(q\in\mathcal Q(c,\vartheta)\), the reference split is \((c_P,\theta_P)\), and its extended-real convention covers zero and singular cells.
statements.justification: The deterministic profile gap is the first proof step that the refuted moving-window localizer lacked.
statements.gap: Porter and Yu (2015) and Tuvaandorj (2020) analyze unknown sharp-RD locations, but do not establish this support-wide false-split gap for a vanishing binary first stage under separate one-sided H\"older constraints.
statements.consumer: The bound converts global cutoff profiling from a heuristic into a certifiable localization device before stochastic calibration is attempted.

statements.statement: Suppose \((c_P,\theta_P)\in\mathcal G_c\times\mathcal G_\vartheta\) and the certified outer margin program contains the true bin averages. Conditional on \(N_1(c_P),\ldots,N_{K_n}(c_P)\), \[P\!\left\{\Delta_n(c_P,\theta_P)>\Gamma_n(\delta_n)\mid N_1(c_P),\ldots,N_{K_n}(c_P)\right\}\le\frac{\delta_n}{|\mathcal G_c||\mathcal G_\vartheta|}\le\delta_n.\] The inequality holds uniformly over every binary conditional treatment--outcome association allowed by \(\mathcal P_n\), including zero joint cells, perfect conditional association, and null-restricted residual variance equal to zero. In the worked grid of \(\text{def:worked-four-cell-grid}\), the displayed vectors equal the bin-averaged law of \(P_0\), their margins have the stated jumps, the population deviance at \((1/2,0)\) is zero, and each fallback branch returns \(\Theta\).
statements.justification: A method-of-types bound calibrates the observed four-cell vector without a covariance eigenvalue condition.
statements.gap: Arai, Hsu, Kitagawa, Mourifi{\'e}, and Wan (2022) show why the joint law matters for fuzzy-RD validity, but do not give an unknown-cutoff profile certificate with arbitrary association nuisance.
statements.consumer: This certificate supplies the honest calibration layer used by every nonfallback branch of the total interval.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{crit}}\), derive the complete \(s=1\) cutoff/effect-label limit experiments separately on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{slope}}\), where \(\tau_n\to\tau\in(0,\infty)\), and on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{entropy},0}\cup\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{entropy},\lambda}\), where \(\tau_n\to\infty\) and \(\lambda_n\to\lambda\in[0,\infty)\). Include boundary-truncated mixtures and every surviving second-order coordinate. Evaluate the fixed-\(\alpha\) minimax expected connected-interval length as \(\mathcal V_\alpha(\tau,\lambda;1)\), and determine whether causal-valid location mixtures together with same-class slope-kink alternatives are least favorable in the full model. Require only the certified reduction \(\mathcal V_\alpha(0,0;1)=2(1-\alpha)\) at the flat boundary; no exact value is asserted on a finite-positive face before the decision problem is solved.
statements.justification: The non-Gaussian decision value, rather than cutoff consistency alone, is the unresolved critical object governing honest interval length.
statements.gap: Elliott and M\"uller (2014) solve a parametric moderate-break process problem and Andrews and Mikusheva (2022) give an abstract weak-GMM decision theory; Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) keep the fuzzy-RD cutoff fixed. None derives this binary H\"older moving-cutoff experiment, its signed causal label, or its connected-length value.
statements.consumer: The value map tells fuzzy-RD users how much interval informativeness remains at each empirically relevant combination of weak compliance and cutoff uncertainty.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{prof}}\), construct \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\) and prove \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\theta_P\in I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\}\ge1-\alpha\] for every strength sequence. On each critical component of \(\mathfrak R\) whose value is evaluated by \(\mathcal V_\alpha\), prove \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}|-L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\longrightarrow0.\] On \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\), prove the lower comparison \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\). Only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\), prove \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}|\asymp L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\asymp r_n.\] The upper comparison must keep the local stochastic contribution \(\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) separate from the remainders \(\zeta_n\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cont},n}\), \(|\mathcal G_c|\exp[-C_{\mathrm{sep}}n\kappa_n^2h_n/4]\), \(2\delta_n\), and twice the maximal probability of each fallback branch in \(\text{def:worked-four-cell-grid}\); the last four expected-length remainders must be \(o(r_n)\), and \(\zeta_n=o(1)\). No upper rate or critical constant is claimed from \(\mathsf{CR}(s,\kappa_\bullet)\), from population separation, or from marginal profiling alone.
statements.justification: A single total interval is needed to turn the limit experiment and lower constructions into uniform frequentist inference.
statements.gap: Andrews and Mikusheva (2016) condition out a functional nuisance in Gaussian-process moment models. Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) and Noack and Rothe (2024) use weak-identification-robust residual-jump inversion at a known cutoff. None supplies a certified four-cell profile or its all-strength minimax length under an unknown cutoff.
statements.consumer: The interval gives a frequentist benchmark for unknown or administratively uncertain eligibility thresholds, including the binary HIV-retention application studied by Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas.

statements.statement: If \(c_P\) is supplied to the rule, suppress cutoff profiling in \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\). The resulting four-cell interval remains honest over the entire known-cutoff restriction of \(\mathcal P_n\), including singular joint laws, and its worst-case expected length is of order \(\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}\). On the subcollection that also satisfies \(\operatorname{Var}_P(Y-\vartheta D\mid X=x)\ge v\) for every \(\vartheta\in\Theta\) and Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in[c_P-1/8,c_P+1/8]\), it is asymptotically equivalent in coverage error and first-order expected length to weak-identification-robust, bias-aware inversion of the null-restricted jump in \(Y-\vartheta D\). No studentized equivalence is asserted on a singular residual face. This is the fixed-cutoff problem studied by Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) and Noack and Rothe (2024); it contains no cutoff-recovery index \(\lambda_n\).
statements.justification: This is the required known-cutoff sanity reduction and guards against efficiency loss from unnecessary global profiling.
statements.gap: Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) develop weak-identification-robust fuzzy-RD inference at a fixed cutoff, and Noack and Rothe (2024) establish honesty for known-cutoff bias-aware inversion. The theorem is a reduction benchmark; the new content lies in the unknown-cutoff regimes.
statements.consumer: Researchers with a reliably documented threshold lose no first-order precision by using the procedure designed for cutoff uncertainty.

sampling_model.design: Independent random design with \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and an unknown law-specific cutoff \(c_P\in[1/4,3/4]\).
sampling_model.units: The observations are \(O_i=(X_i,D_i,Y_i)\), for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with binary treatment and outcome.
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument is \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge c_P\}\), and monotone response types imply \(D_i=D_i(Z_i)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The compliance jump lies in \([\kappa_n,2\kappa_n]\). The main class imposes no outcome-variance, residual-variance, covariance-eigenvalue, or joint-cell positivity floor; every binary treatment--outcome association compatible with the observable margins and causal model is allowed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Separate one-sided radius-\(M\), order-\(s\) H\"older extensions are imposed only on the observable treatment and outcome margins. Association is a free binwise Fr\'echet coordinate. A four-cell method-of-types threshold gives finite-sample calibration on certified grids, and the rule returns the full parameter space on each enumerated fallback branch.

estimand_functional: \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}=\operatorname{hull}\{\vartheta\in\Theta:\inf_{c\in\mathcal G_c}\Delta_n(c,\vartheta)\le\Gamma_n(\delta_n)\},\quad L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\asymp r_n\text{ by the proposed upper comparison only on }\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Theorem 1 establishes honesty of the bias-aware Anderson--Rubin confidence set at a known cutoff.
Their weak-identification-robust fuzzy-RD procedure inverts a reduced-form test at a fixed known cutoff.
Their unknown-threshold result transfers the minimax rate for estimating a sharp-RD discontinuity location from a convolution white-noise model.
Their moderate-break analysis derives a Gaussian-process limit experiment and a nearly weighted-average-power maximizing test.
Their Theorem 1 gives uniformly asymptotically valid conditional tests with a functional nuisance parameter.
Their Theorem 1 shows that risk functions attainable in the weak-GMM Gaussian-process experiment bound finite-sample asymptotic risk.
Their Theorem 3.1 characterizes optimal one-sided confidence intervals through an ordered modulus over convex fixed-index regression classes.
Their sharp testable implications for fuzzy-RD validity are inequalities in the joint outcome--treatment distribution at the cutoff.
Their LoTTA model propagates posterior uncertainty about an unknown cutoff into fuzzy-RD effect estimation.
Their main unknown-discontinuity theory treats testing and estimation in sharp RD, with fuzzy RD discussed separately.

tldr: For fuzzy regression discontinuity with a weak compliance jump and unknown cutoff, cutoff recovery and causal-effect informativeness are distinct. A legal moving-cutoff continuum yields the exact flat-face limit \(2(1-\alpha)\), while \(T_n\), \(\tau_n\), and \(\lambda_n\) give an explicit all-strength regime partition. The open kernel is the \(s=1\) critical decision value and a total support-wide interval based on a formally defined four-cell population profile. Finite-grid honesty covers every compatible treatment--outcome association, including singular cells; the conservative procedure's upper rate is posed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\), where its named grid, sieve, stochastic, continuum-transfer, calibration, and fallback errors are negligible.

project_justification.gap: Known-cutoff weak-fuzzy inference, sharp-RD unknown-cutoff rates, generic weak-identification decision theory, and Bayesian propagation of cutoff uncertainty have been developed separately. None characterizes honest connected-interval length when the cutoff and fuzzy denominator weaken jointly.
project_justification.niche: The preserved binary uniform-design class makes the causal lift explicit while leaving the observable treatment--outcome association unrestricted. This creates a nonregular location/effect decision problem that is neither a fixed-boundary modulus problem nor a parametric unknown-break problem.
project_justification.fill: The project couples a legal moving-cutoff continuum with a support-wide four-cell population profile and a coarsened exact calibration that leaves association free. It evaluates the critical decision problems and seeks a total honest interval, with its conservative finite-grid upper-rate claim confined to the explicitly certifiable recovered regime.

related_work: Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001) supply the local Wald identification argument. Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) are the direct weak-identification fuzzy-RD predecessor: their reduced-form inversion treats the assignment cutoff as fixed and known, so there is no cutoff/effect-label experiment or unknown-cutoff minimax connected-length problem. Noack and Rothe (2024, Theorem 1 and Assumption 1(iii)) add honest bias-aware inversion for \(Y-\theta D\), also at a known cutoff; their variance and correlation conditions suffice to studentize \(Y-cD\), whereas the comparison subclass here states the required null-residual variance directly and the main four-cell class imposes no such floor. Porter and Yu (2015, Sections 3--5) and Tuvaandorj (2020, Sections 3--4) inform unknown-location analysis in predominantly sharp designs, without the weak causal ratio. Elliott and M\"uller (2014, Sections 2.1--2.3) show why moderate unknown breaks require a process experiment, but their parametric break problem has no H\"older recovery profile. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016, equations (3)--(4) and Theorem 1) and Andrews and Mikusheva (2022, Theorem 1 and Section 4) inform nuisance calibration and weak-decision analysis. Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.4) connect testing power to expected length over convex fixed-index classes; the cutoff-indexed class here is a translated nonconvex union. Arai, Hsu, Kitagawa, Mourifi{\'e}, and Wan (2022, Section 2) establish that fuzzy-RD validity restrictions reside in the joint outcome--treatment law, motivating retention of all four observed cells. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version, Sections 3 and 6) propagate unknown-cutoff uncertainty in a Bayesian model without uniform frequentist honesty or minimax length.
technical_internal_limitation: A product of the two marginal Bernoulli likelihoods is not the likelihood of the observed pair when association is unrestricted. The finite-grid calibration therefore uses the complete binned four-cell vector and a method-of-types threshold that remains valid on singular cell faces. Its dimension cost \(\zeta_n\) need not be negligible on every sequence satisfying cutoff recovery; the stated upper-rate comparison is therefore confined to \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\), while a sharper association-robust calibration for the remainder of \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\) stays open. Separately, an untruncated second moment of a translated-cutoff mixture does not determine a critical constant; boundary truncation, mixture renormalization, the signed effect label, and second-order centering must remain in the experiment.
honest_scope: The main class has no outcome-variance or null-residual-variance floor. The direct condition on \(\operatorname{Var}(Y-\vartheta D\mid X=x)\) applies only to the studentized known-cutoff equivalence and uses a Lebesgue-almost-everywhere convention. The moving-cutoff continuum, its causal lift, the finite-sample Kullback--Leibler bound, the flat-face expected-length limit, the algebraic regime partition, the population profile separation, and finite-grid four-cell calibration are explicit claims to prove. The finite-positive decision values, full-model least favorability, continuum discretization, negligible fallback risk, and all-strength attainment are open-ended questions. The minimax lower comparison at scale \(r_n\) is posed on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\); the conservative finite-grid upper comparison is posed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\). No smoothness of joint cells, conditional independence, association separation, cross-side derivative matching, oracle cutoff, or known association nuisance is imposed.
novelty_justification: Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer and Noack and Rothe establish weak-fuzzy inference with a fixed known cutoff. Tuvaandorj develops unknown-location rate theory without a weak causal ratio or connected-length loss. Elliott and M\"uller and Andrews and Mikusheva provide experiment and decision templates without deriving this binary H\"older problem. The strict unresolved delta is the cutoff/effect-label decision value and a single total interval attaining it across the explicit regime partition. The association contribution is narrower and settled at the calibration layer: a four-cell finite-grid certificate is valid for every compatible binary association, while critical efficiency and continuum transfer remain to be proved.
message: Revised core adds the exact null-residual comparison condition, formal four-cell population loss, noncircular separation constant, explicit grid and sieve schedules, and named stochastic, continuum-transfer, calibration, and fallback errors.
